Intelligent Research Assistant
Project Report
6
User Interface Design (UX/UI)
The frontend of the Intelligent Research Assistant was designed with a heavy emphasis
on premium aesthetics and psychological engagement. Recognizing that research tools
are often visually sterile and utilitarian, this project adopted a modern Glassmorphism
design language.
6.1
The Glassmorphism Aesthetic
Glassmorphism is characterized by semi-transparent backgrounds with a distinct background-
blur effect, creating the illusion of floating frosted glass. This was achieved using advanced
CSS3 properties:
1 .glass -panel {

This effect adds depth to the application, distinguishing foreground interactive ele-
ments (like chat boxes and workspace cards) from the subtle, animated grid background.
6.2
Micro-Animations and Tactile Feedback
User experience is heavily defined by how the system reacts to user input. Every button,
input field, and navigation link features custom cubic-bezier transition curves.
For instance, when a user hovers over a primary button or a workspace card, the
element elegantly scales up and projects a colored drop-shadow:
1 .btn -primary {
2
transition: all 0.3s cubic -bezier (0.16 , 1, 0.3, 1);
3 }
